scenarios.notes: Control game SL-CHN-SAM01 (Flashpoint, China, Scarborough). Played 4 months. Verdict: visibly crafted art and type, but a dense desk with number mismatches and a choose-all-then-execute loop that feels like clicking through.
steps: Title: Play a seed, typed SL-CHN-SAM01, started
Month 1 desk, chose two recommended orders and a crisis answer, skipped the mission move
Month 2 desk, choose all recommended, then Map mode, added Court Philippines from the map
Month 3 desk, choose all recommended, execute
Month 4 result card and What happened recap

scenarios.notes: Compared the same order on desk (Choose, diamond cost) and map (Add to this month, coin icons, ORDERED stamp). Same outcome, different wording and idiom.
steps: Desk: mission order card with Choose button
Map: tapped Philippines, order cards with Add to this month
Added Court Philippines from the map and executed

friction.where: Month 1 desk, third crisis answer card (Pause and express regret)
friction.expected: Recommendation line sits inside the card with padding
friction.happened: The 'Recommended by your Finance Minister and your Chief of Staff' text overflows above the card top edge and the last line ('mission.') clips at the bottom; the card is cramped compared with the two above. Reference: Suzerain keeps text in fixed frames.

Header says 'Political capital (what orders cost) 3 of 6', then 'Orders 0 of 6', then 'Your calls 2 open'; left rail says '3 things'; right panel says '3 now, nothing spent'. Five counters for three tasks.

friction.expected: Pressing the lowest Choose picks the crisis answer
friction.happened: I pressed the 3rd 'Choose' and it hit 'Choose all recommended' in the right panel, which committed two orders I had not read. The controls share the label and look.

friction.expected: The big number matches the small ones
friction.happened: Big stamp says 'Approval -6'; the details line says approval 64 to 62 (-2). Mission line says Manila -65 to -56, the row below says -65 to -57 (+8).
Header pill '4 of 6' while the right panel says '5 now, 1 spent, 4 left'. Month 4 result: header '6 of 6', result card '5 to 4 (-1)'.
Choice card: 'at a cost: Stability -3'. Tile below: Stability -2. Header: 77 down 2.

friction.where: Skip card wording, month 1 vs month 2
friction.happened: Month 1: 'Leave it open: the crisis passes with no effect'. Month 2: 'Skip for now: your cabinet decides'. Same Skip button, opposite outcome. The mission card calls it 'Hold this month'.
'Your call' labels a crisis, a mission move, and the header counter 'Your calls 2 open'. 'Mission', 'goal' and 'Your goal' are three words for one thing; 'goals on track 2 of 4' vs 'All goals (6)'.

friction.expected: Same action looks and reads like the desk
friction.happened: Desk says 'Choose' with a diamond cost; map says 'Add to this month' with coin icons, an ORDERED stamp and 'Your choice' badge; the left panel jumps back to card 1 after adding. Map markers are all unlabelled 'Map marker'. The decided list collapses to a comma sentence with 'Show' instead of per-item Change buttons.
'Mass troops facing Philippines' shows 'free' and '6% defense', 'Spy' shows '95% chance'; nothing says what each figure is.
'Condemn publicly' and 'Reinforce and shadow them' show identical effect text ('Approval up. Taiwan's view of you down.'), so the choice reads as flavour.

friction.expected: Choice visible from the top of the page
friction.happened: The page opened scrolled so the title was cut off. 'Some help' is pre-selected as recommended and I kept it. The explanations are legible and out of the way.

friction.where: Names: Scarborough Shoal, Mutual Defense Treaty, Sara Duterte, Lai Ching-te, Shehbaz Sharif
friction.expected: Known from general news or explained
friction.happened: Scarborough Shoal and Sara Duterte were new; the 'Who is who' strip and 'i names' chips explained them in one line, which worked and stayed out of the way.
A one-party state leader gets 'We will remember at the ballot box' attributed to 'On the street'. Reads as template text.

bugs.title: Recommendation text overflows crisis answer card
steps: Look at the third answer card of 'How fast to pour'
bugs.actual: Recommendation text pokes out over the card border above; last line clipped

bugs.title: Result numbers disagree within one card
steps: Month 1: choose Pause and express regret, Execute
Compare the Approval stamp, the details line and the header
bugs.expected: Approval and Philippines relation changes match everywhere
bugs.actual: Approval -6 stamp vs -2 in details; relation -56 vs -57

bugs.title: Political capital shown differently in header and side panel
steps: Compare header pill and 'If you execute now'

suggestions.what: One resource counter in the header (capital left this month); fold the Orders, Meetings, Defense and Calls counters into a single tray
Give 'Choose all recommended' a distinct treatment and say what it commits
Use the map's order card idiom and wording on the desk, or the reverse, so the same order reads the same
Reconcile every delta on a result card from one source (stamp, details, tiles, header)
Label map markers with country names on hover and for screen readers

delight: The title globe with the 'Pick a fire' serif headline and the live ticker: real art direction (sessions/sam-desktop/001-title.png)
Seed code entry worked first time and the briefing is tidy (003-afterseed.png)
Result cards with illustrated scenes, serif headline and the DONE stamp; the ORDERED stamp on the map (009-r1.png, 015-r2.png, 017-r3.png)
Map order cards with icons are more characterful than the desk's text cards (013-map2.png)

fun.reason: Four months in I was approving the staff's picks; the result cards are fun to see, the decisions are not yet tense.

clarity.reason: Plenty of explanation, but five counters for one resource and disagreeing numbers undermine it.

visual.reason: Title, result illustrations and typography are crafted; cramped cards, an overflow and a text-heavy desk drag it down.

feels_like_a_game.reason: The title and result scenes feel authored; the desk feels like an admin panel with Choose buttons.

agency.reason: I always knew what to press, but 'Choose all recommended' then Execute makes my input nearly optional, and Skip means different things.

realism.reason: Plausible Scarborough dynamics, but a one-party leader quoted about ballot boxes felt templated.

replay.reason: I would not start a second run until the numbers agree; I did not play a second game.

recommend.reason: I would tell a friend the art is better than they expect, with a warning that the UI is busy. Not yet 'crafted game', no longer 'AI dashboard'.

quit_point: Month 3 (Jan 2027) desk: after pressing Choose all recommended and Execute without reading a card, I realised the loop was clicking through, and the capital counters disagreed again. I played one more month to finish the record.
verbatim: Better than I expected from a title screen, and then the desk turned into a form. Pick one number for my political capital and make every screen agree with it.
